cpContext.applyGeneratedLines: Apply the generated lines from this tool.

completion.alreadyClosed: This vertex already folds consistently — no crease is missing.
completion.boundaryVertex: This point is on the edge of the paper, so there is nothing to close — pick a vertex inside the sheet.
completion.creasesDoNotMeet: These creases do not all meet at one point, so there is no single vertex to close.
completion.exceedsFullFold: No single crease can close this vertex: it would have to fold past 180°.
completion.forcedMountain: This crease has to be a mountain — drawn as one, not in the selected line type.
completion.forcedValley: This crease has to be a valley — drawn as one, not in the selected line type.
completion.indeterminate: Cannot tell: a crease here is unassigned, or another crease passes through without ending here.
completion.overdetermined: No single crease closes this vertex — at least two would be needed.
completion.tooManyUnknowns: Another crease here has no fold angle yet, so there is more than one unknown too many. Give it an angle, or run Solve Undecided Creases.

cpContext.dragAcrossCreases: Drag across creases to apply this action.
cpContext.foldAngleUnassignedDescription: Leave the fold angle undecided, keeping mountain or valley
cpContext.foldDirectionMountainDescription: Remember that these undecided creases folded as mountains
cpContext.foldDirectionNoneDescription: Forget which way these undecided creases folded
cpContext.foldDirectionValleyDescription: Remember that these undecided creases folded as valleys

insertVertex.noCreaseThroughPoint: No crease passes through this point, so there is no vertex to insert. Aim at a crossing, or at a point on a crease.

cpContext.measureClearHint: Backspace removes the last, Escape clears all

propagation.answeredFlat: These creases were worked out and they do not fold, so there is no angle to set. They stay unassigned.
propagation.conflicts: Vertices that no longer close: {{vertices}} — something this rests on disagrees.
propagation.noComponentAtPoint: Nothing to solve here. Click on a crease or a vertex of the pattern you want.
propagation.noScope: Click a crease or vertex to solve outward from, or select the creases to solve.
propagation.nothingDecidable: Nothing could be worked out from the angles already set. Give one more crease an angle and try again.
propagation.nothingFree: Every crease already has a fold angle. Make some unassigned first, then solve.
propagation.nothingInScope: The selection no longer names any creases. Select some again, or clear the selection and click a pattern.
propagation.outOfScope: Vertices needing creases you did not select: {{vertices}} — select those too, or clear the selection and click the pattern.
propagation.selectionNothingFree: Every crease in the selection already has a fold angle. Select some unassigned creases, or clear the selection and click a pattern.

cpContext.resetSettingsHint: A setting here is not its default. Some settings are remembered between sessions.

solveAngles.againstHint: This folds a crease the opposite way from the direction remembered for it — applying replaces that.
solveAngles.creaseNotInFan: Pick three different creases that all meet at the same vertex.
solveAngles.current: This is what the vertex already does — step to see the alternative.
solveAngles.family: These three creases leave one degree of freedom, so this is one of infinitely many answers — pick a different third crease for a definite one.
solveAngles.leavesUndecided: This answer does not fold one of the creases at all, so it stays undecided — step to see an answer that decides all three.
solveAngles.notEnoughCreases: Fewer than three creases meet here, so there are no three angles to solve.
solveAngles.title: Fold angles
solveAngles.unreachable: These three creases cannot close this vertex at any fold angles — try a different three.

cpContext.squareLineTypeActiveHint: Draw the square in the active line type
cpContext.squareLineTypeEdgeHint: Always draw the square as edges
cpContext.squareUnitPaperHint: Size as a fraction of the paper edge
cpContext.stopOnAuxAria: Let a suggested crease stop at an auxiliary line

cpRail.openEditableFirst: Open an editable crease pattern first

creaseAngle.fieldTitle: Fold angle given to new mountain and valley creases
creaseAngle.title: Crease angle

divideMode.countTitle: Divide the line into equal parts
divideMode.ratioTitle: Divide the line at a ratio

noKeys.emergent: More than one fourth crease lets these creases lie flat. Step through them.
noKeys.opening: The flap opens more than one way: the lit layers stay together. Step through them.
noKeys.order: The layers can land stacked more than one way. Step through them.
noKeys.pocket: The point can sink into more than one pocket between its layers. Step through them.
noKeys.ridge: Either ridge lets the swivel lie flat. Step through them.
noKeys.root: This axiom has more than one fold here. Step through them.
noKeys.target: More than one layer takes the tuck: the brightest is the one taken. Step through them.

withKeys.emergent: More than one fourth crease lets these creases lie flat. Step through them, or press {{keys}}.
withKeys.opening: The flap opens more than one way: the lit layers stay together. Step through them, or press {{keys}}.
withKeys.order: The layers can land stacked more than one way. Step through them, or press {{keys}}.
withKeys.pocket: The point can sink into more than one pocket between its layers. Step through them, or press {{keys}}.
withKeys.ridge: Either ridge lets the swivel lie flat. Step through them, or press {{keys}}.
withKeys.root: This axiom has more than one fold here. Step through them, or press {{keys}}.
withKeys.target: More than one layer takes the tuck: the brightest is the one taken. Step through them, or press {{keys}}.

crimp.bothFit: Both kinds of crimp fit here: choose which way the tip goes.
crimp.firstLineAxiom: The first line is located by {{mode}}, the line mode in hand. To draw it, choose Free line under First line.
crimp.intro: Folds a flap in along a first line and back out along a second, so its end turns. Draw the first line nearer the body and the second nearer the tip; each runs across the flap.
crimp.onlyInside: Only the inside crimp fits here.
crimp.onlyOutside: Only the outside crimp fits here.

extent.keyNote: Press {{shortcut}} to step through the extents.
extent.label: Extent
extent.pinchHelp: Crease only a short mark, centred on a point you click along the line.
extent.segmentHelp: Crease the line only between two points you click along it.
extent.wholeHelp: Crease the line from edge to edge.

fix.foldOntoLine: Fold the edge onto the line instead
fix.slideToEdge: Slide the line to land the point on the edge
fix.tuckOverAnother: Tuck over the layer that fits instead
fix.tuckUnderAnother: Tuck under the layer that fits instead
fix.turnToEdge: Turn the line to land the point on the edge

flap.chipAdded_one: Flap {{number}}, {{count}} layer, moves with the fold
flap.chipAdded_other: Flap {{number}}, {{count}} layers, moves with the fold
flap.name: Flap {{number}}

line.axiom2Help: The line that folds one point onto another.
line.axiom3Help: The line that folds one edge or crease onto another.
line.axiom4Help: The line through a point, perpendicular to an edge or crease.
line.axiom5Help: The line through a pivot that folds a point onto an edge or crease.
line.axiom6Help: The line that folds two points onto two edges or creases at once.
line.axiom7Help: The line that folds a point onto an edge or crease, perpendicular to another.
line.creaseHelp: A crease or folded edge already there: refold a precrease, or unfold a flap.
line.freeHelp: A line drawn anywhere, with no reference.

note.acrossLayers: These points lie on layers that are folded apart, so the line runs through them where they lie in the folded form. The crease pattern shows the creases it makes.
note.along: Points snap to where the line crosses creases, edges and marks, to points on it, and to its middle.
note.alongBack: Esc takes back the last point.
note.closedSinkLine: The line across the point sets how deep it sinks.
note.crease: Folding along a precrease refolds it; along a folded edge, it unfolds the flap.
note.divide: Edges, folded edges and precreases all count.
note.free: No snapping: the line runs exactly through the points you click.
note.freePoint: Hold {{modifier}} to put a point down anywhere, without snapping.
note.openSinkLine: The line across the point sets how deep it sinks, and must be exactly square to its centre line. Axiom 4, through a point and perpendicular to the centre crease, gives one that is.
note.queued: Folding as soon as the preview is ready…
note.rotateCancel: Esc puts Rotate down without adding the turn.
note.rotatePreview: The folded pane shows the model turned as it will be.
note.rotateRefused: This turn cannot be added here.
note.severalSunk_one: {{count}} sunk point lies here: the first is taken.
note.severalSunk_other: {{count}} sunk points lie here: the first is taken.
note.snap: Points snap to corners, marks, crease crossings, midpoints and edges.
note.unsinkLine: Locate the ring the sink left: Existing crease takes a crease of it along the sunk point’s top.

fold.plannedPleat: Not a tool of its own: fold a pleat as two plain folds, a valley and then a mountain beside it.
fold.plannedReason: Planned: not in Ori Studio yet.

readOnly.locked: This step is from a newer Ori Studio, so nothing can be folded from it.
readOnly.newer: This sequence is from a newer Ori Studio, so it opens read-only.

budget.text: Working out how the layers stack took too long here, so it is not known whether this fold fits. Fold fewer layers, or fold it elsewhere.
budget.title: The search ran out of time

choiceBroken.text: The opening or the layer order this step stored no longer fits the paper before it, so it cannot be folded as it is stored.
choiceBroken.title: A choice no longer fits

chooseOpening.text: The flap opens more than one way. Pick one to fold.
chooseOpening.title: Choose how it opens

chooseOrder.text: The fold can land with its layers stacked more than one way. Pick one to fold.
chooseOrder.title: Choose how the layers stack

choosePocket.text: The point can sink into more than one pocket between its layers. Pick one to fold.
choosePocket.title: Choose a pocket

closureAddsFlaps.textMany_one: Folding these layers moves {{count}} more flap too.
closureAddsFlaps.textMany_other: Folding these layers moves {{count}} more flaps too.
closureAddsFlaps.textOne: Folding these layers moves flap {{number}} too.
closureAddsFlaps.title: More flaps would move

collision.text: The moving layers would pass through layers in their way.
collision.title: Collision

crimpKindInfeasible.neitherRedraw: Neither an inside nor an outside crimp fits these lines: no way of stacking the layers lets the tip turn on both. Press Esc and draw the lines closer to parallel, or crimp fewer flaps.
crimpKindInfeasible.text: No way of stacking the layers lets the tip turn this way on both lines. The other kind of crimp may fit.

crimpLinesMeet.redraw: The two lines cross, or come too close, over the paper the crimp moves. Press Esc and draw the second line clear of the first, all the way across the flap.
crimpLinesMeet.title: The lines meet

crimpMissesTip.redraw: The second line crosses none of the paper beyond the first, so nothing would turn back. Swap the tip side if the tip is the other end, or press Esc and draw the second line across the flap, beyond the first.
crimpMissesTip.title: The second line misses the flap

crimpNoOpening.noSpine: A single layer has no folded edge to crimp along. Crimp a flap of layers joined by a fold.
crimpNoOpening.text: Its layers part at the first line, but at the second one of them has ended, or has nothing to turn on. Move the second line, or crimp other flaps.
crimpNoOpening.title: This flap cannot open at the second line

crimpOutsideInfeasible.title: It cannot crimp round the outside

crimpTipNotFree.text: Other layers lie where the crimped paper would turn. Include their flaps in the crimp, or crimp it somewhere else.

emptySeed.text: No layer is picked. Pick at least one flap to move.
emptySeed.title: Nothing to fold

extentMissesLayers.text: None of the layers this precrease goes through lies along that stretch of the line, or the line is creased there already. Click points elsewhere along the line, or crease through all layers.
extentMissesLayers.title: No layer to crease there

extentMissesPaper.text: That stretch of the line runs over no paper, so there is nothing to crease. Click points where the line crosses the paper.
extentMissesPaper.title: No paper there

extentOffPaper.text: A point the crease is measured from does not lie on the paper as it is folded now. Click its points along the line where the line crosses the paper.
extentOffPaper.title: A point is off the paper

extentTooShort.pinch: This pinch is too short for the paper to take a crease. Crease more of the line.
extentTooShort.segment: The two points are too close together along the line to crease between them. Click two points farther apart, or pinch there instead.
extentTooShort.title: Too short to crease

invalid.text: It would not land on a valid flat model.
invalid.title: This fold cannot be made

kindInfeasible.neither: Neither kind of reverse fold fits here: no way of stacking the layers lets the tip turn. Move the line, or reverse other flaps.
kindInfeasible.text: No way of stacking the layers lets the tip turn this way here. The other kind of reverse fold may fit.

markOffSheet.text: Part of the mark would lie off the sheet. Click its points along the line inside the paper.
markOffSheet.title: The mark would leave the paper

markOnCrease.text: The mark would lie along a crease that is already there. Mark another stretch of the line, or fold along the crease itself.
markOnCrease.title: Already creased there

marksOverlap.text: The mark would lie over part of a mark made before, in a way the paper cannot take. Mark another stretch of the line, or crease the whole line.
marksOverlap.title: The marks would overlap

markTooShort.text: On one of its layers the mark would be too short for the paper to take a crease. Crease more of the line.
markTooShort.title: Too short to crease

moverStays.text: The layer that carries the point to move is not among the layers folding. Include its flap, or fold every layer.
moverStays.title: The point would stay put

nearMiss.text: The line passes just beside a point of the paper: too close to fold cleanly, too far to go through it.
nearMiss.title: Too close to a point

noMovingSide.text: No paper lies on the side of the line that would move. Swap the moving side, or move the line onto the paper.
noMovingSide.title: Nothing to fold

noRoot.text: These references give no fold line on the paper as it is folded. Pick other references.
noRoot.title: No fold here

noSide.text: Nothing says which side of the line moves. Pick a point off the line, on the side to move.
noSide.title: Which side moves?

nothingStays.text: Every layer is on the moving side, so nothing would stay put. Pick a flap to fold.
nothingStays.title: Everything would move

offPaper.text: A point or edge the line was located from does not lie on the paper as it is folded now. Locate the line again.
offPaper.title: A reference is not on the paper

outsideInfeasible.title: It cannot wrap round the outside

pickAgain.text: That spot is not inside a layer on the moving side. Pick inside a layer, away from its creases.
pickAgain.title: Pick again

pointsTooClose.text: The two points land in the same place on the folded paper, so they make no line. Pick two points farther apart.
pointsTooClose.title: The points are too close

precreaseUnfold.text: Unfolding it would move more layers than folding it did.
precreaseUnfold.title: This precrease cannot unfold

reverseNoOpening.bodiesCross: Parted along its folds, the paper each half hangs on would cross the other’s.
reverseNoOpening.noBody: Parted along its folds, one half would hang on nothing that stays put at the line.
reverseNoOpening.noSpine: A single layer has no folded edge to reverse along. Reverse a flap of layers joined by a fold.
reverseNoOpening.noSplit: Its layers cannot be parted along a fold without a lower layer ending up over an upper one.
reverseNoOpening.title: This flap cannot open

sinkLineTilted.text: An open sink needs the line exactly square to the point’s centre line: tilted even a little, the point cannot open-sink. The square line at the same depth can.
sinkLineTilted.title: The line is not square to the point

sinkNoAxis.text: Its outside does not run along two straight sides, so there is no centre line for an open sink’s line to be square to.
sinkNoAxis.title: The point has no centre line

sinkNoOrder.none: No way of stacking the layers lets the point sink this way here. Move the line, or pick another point.
sinkNoOrder.otherSink: No way of stacking the layers lets the point sink this way here. The other kind of sink fits.
sinkNoOrder.title: The point cannot sink this way here
sinkNoOrder.unsink: No way of stacking the layers lets the sunk point come back out here.
sinkNoOrder.unsinkTitle: The point cannot come back out here

sinkNoPocket.text: No gap between its layers runs the whole way round its outside for the tip to go into, so it cannot closed-sink.
sinkNoPocket.title: The point has no pocket

sinkOutlineMixed.text: The point’s outside edges are mountain folds and valley folds both: it has no one outside to turn inside out, so it cannot open-sink.
sinkOutlineMixed.title: Its outside is not one fold

sinkPointOpen.text: Raw edges reach its tip: its layers are free corners, not a closed point, so nothing says how they would sink. Sink a point whose layers are joined at the tip.
sinkPointOpen.title: The point is open

sinkSeveralPoints.text_one: {{count}} point lies on the tip side, and a sink takes one. Pick the point to sink.
sinkSeveralPoints.text_other: {{count}} points lie on the tip side, and a sink takes one. Pick the point to sink.
sinkSeveralPoints.title: Pick one point

sliver.text: A point of the moving layers would land a hair’s breadth inside another layer’s edge.
sliver.title: A point lands just inside an edge

tipNotFree.text: Other layers lie where the tip would turn. Include their flaps in the fold, or reverse it somewhere else.
tipNotFree.title: Layers are in the way

tooSmall.text: The fold would leave a crease or a strip of paper thinner than the paper itself.
tooSmall.title: Too small to fold

tuckInfeasible.none: No way of stacking the layers puts the flap right against that layer. Tuck fewer flaps, or locate another line.
tuckInfeasible.text: No way of stacking the layers puts the flap right against that layer. Another layer here takes it.
tuckInfeasible.titleOver: It cannot be tucked over that layer
tuckInfeasible.titleUnder: It cannot be tucked under that layer

tuckNoTarget.over: No layer that stays can take the flap over it here. Fold it the other way, swap the moving side, or locate another line.
tuckNoTarget.title: No layer takes the tuck here
tuckNoTarget.under: No layer that stays can take the flap under it here. Fold it the other way, swap the moving side, or locate another line.

tuckTarget.text: Pick a layer that stays put to tuck the flap against.
tuckTarget.title: The layer to tuck under would move

unsinkNotSunk.text: Nothing sunk lies inside the paper along this line. Locate the ring a sink left, and pick the sunk point inside it.
unsinkNotSunk.title: No sunk point here

unsupported.text: This version of Ori Studio cannot fold it as it is stored.
unsupported.title: This step cannot be folded

wrongCrease.text: Unfold along a folded edge, and refold along a flat crease.
wrongCrease.title: Not that kind of crease

reverse.bothFit: Both kinds fit here: choose which way the tip goes.
reverse.onlyInside: Only the inside reverse fold fits here.
reverse.onlyOutside: Only the outside reverse fold fits here.

section.label: Layers at the fold line, top to bottom
section.labelWoven: Layers at the fold line under the pointer, top to bottom
section.rowAddedBeside: Layer {{layer}}, {{flap}}, moves with the fold, beside layer {{above}}

sink.bothFit: Both sinks fit here: an open sink turns every layer inside out, a closed one keeps them together.
sink.depthHelp: How far the line lies from the point’s tip along its centre line, the paper’s side being 1. Locate the line farther down to sink the point deeper.
sink.neither: Neither sink fits this point here.
sink.onlyClosed: Only the closed sink fits here.
sink.onlyOpen: Only the open sink fits here.
sink.squareNote: An open sink needs the line exactly square to the point’s centre line: tilted even a little, the point cannot open-sink. A closed sink takes a tilted line.

steps.axiom1First: Click the first point the fold passes through.
steps.axiom3Move: Click the edge or crease to move.
steps.axiom3Onto: Click the edge or crease to lay it on.
steps.axiom4Through: Click the point the fold passes through.
steps.axiom5Pivot: Click the pivot the fold passes through.
steps.axiom6FirstPoint: Click the first point to move.
steps.axiom6SecondLine: Click the edge or crease that one should land on.
steps.axiom6SecondPoint: Click the second point to move.
steps.commitOrClick: Press Enter, or click {{action}}, to fold.
steps.crease: Click the crease or folded edge to fold along.
steps.crimpFinish: Choose Inside or Outside, then press Enter.
steps.crimpFinishTouch: Choose Inside or Outside, then tap {{action}}.
steps.crimpFirstCrease: Click the crease or folded edge where the flap turns in.
steps.crimpFirstStart: Click where the first line starts, nearer the body: where the flap turns in.
steps.crimpKind: Choose Inside to tuck the paper between the lines inside the flap, or Outside to wrap it round the flap; a kind that does not fit is greyed out.
steps.crimpLayers: Under Layers, leave out any flap that should not crimp.
steps.crimpSecondCrease: Click the crease or folded edge beyond the first line where the flap turns back out.
steps.crimpSecondStart: Click where the second line starts, beyond the first toward the tip: where the flap turns back out.
steps.crimpTip: The end beyond the second line is the tip, which turns: if it is the wrong end, Swap the tip side.
steps.divide: Click an edge or crease to divide it.
steps.divideUse: Use the new points as references for any fold.
steps.finish: Pick the fold and the layers, then press Enter.
steps.finishTouch: Pick the fold and the layers, then tap {{action}}.
steps.freeStart: Click where the fold line starts.
steps.landOnLine: Click the edge or crease it should land on.
steps.perpendicularTo: Click the edge or crease the fold is perpendicular to.
steps.pickPoint: Pick which point sinks: a sink takes one.
steps.pickSunkPoint: The sunk point is found for you: pick another in the layers to pull that out.
steps.pickTuckTarget: Pick the layer to tuck against.
steps.pinchAt: Click where to pinch along the line.
steps.rotateAmount: Choose how far to turn the model: a part of a turn, or an exact angle.
steps.rotateCommit: Press Enter to add the turn.
steps.segmentFrom: Click where the crease starts along the line.

tool.closedSinkHelp: Push a closed point’s tip into a pocket, its layers kept together.
tool.crimpHelp: Fold a flap in along one line and back out along a second, so its end turns.
tool.divideLineHelp: Mark points that divide an edge or a crease into equal parts.
tool.insideReverseHelp: Push a flap inside itself, reversing its spine.
tool.mountainHelp: Fold the moving side away from you, so it lands underneath.
tool.openSinkHelp: Push a closed point’s tip in, turning every layer of it inside out.
tool.precreaseHelp: Fold and unfold, leaving a crease to use later.
tool.rotateHelp: Turn the model round by a part of a turn or an exact angle, previewed, then applied as a step of its own.
tool.tuckHelp: Fold a flap and slide it under, or over, a layer that stays.
tool.unsinkHelp: Pull a sunk point’s tip back out.
tool.valleyHelp: Fold the moving side toward you, so it lands on top.

tuck.noTargets: No layer here takes the tuck.
tuck.targetsOver_one: One layer here takes the tuck over it.
tuck.targetsOver_other: {{count}} layers here take the tuck over them: the folded paper lights each.
tuck.targetsUnder_one: One layer here takes the tuck under it.
tuck.targetsUnder_other: {{count}} layers here take the tuck under them: the folded paper lights each.

verb.turnOverHelp: Turn the model over, side to side, as a step of its own.

fix.creaseKites: Crease the kites as it folds
fix.emergent: Use the fourth crease that fits
fix.resetTarget: Put the spine onto the hinge

vertex.fourthsFit_one: One fourth crease fits with this paper staying put.
vertex.fourthsFit_other: {{count}} fourth creases fit with this paper staying put.

help.petalHinge: Lift a flap’s lower point along a hinge while its sides fold in along two kite creases.
help.rabbitEar: Fold a triangle’s corners in along their bisectors, so a point stands up.
help.squash: Open a two-layer flap and press it flat, its spine onto its hinge.
help.swivelEdge: Swivel an edge onto a line, pivoting at a point.

intro.petalHinge: Lifts a flap’s lower point up along a hinge while its sides fold in along two kite creases. Select the hinge as a crease already across the flap, or by its two ends: then the fold creases the hinge through the top layer, and any kite crease that is missing, as it folds.
intro.swivelEdge: Swivels an edge onto a line, pivoting at a point. The creases meet where the pivot sits, moved onto the line halfway between the edge and the line it lands on, and the paper between them turns flat.

lineBy.creaseOrEdgeHelp: Click a crease or an edge already there
lineBy.hingeCreaseHelp: Click a precrease already across the flap
lineBy.twoEndpointsHelp: Click the hinge’s two ends: the fold creases it
lineBy.twoPointsHelp: Click two points on the line

vertex.mountainTitle: Mountain: the paper turns away from you
vertex.noFourth: No fourth crease fits with this paper staying put: click other paper to stay.
vertex.noFourthAnywhere: No fourth crease fits these creases, whichever paper stays: press Esc and pick again.
vertex.noFourthAnywhereTouch: No fourth crease fits these creases, whichever paper stays: tap Cancel and pick again.
vertex.noFourthTouch: No fourth crease fits with this paper staying put: tap other paper to stay.

note.freePoint: Hold {{modifier}} to put a point anywhere.
note.freePointTouch: Turn on Free point to put a point anywhere.
note.petalCreasesAll: The fold creases the hinge through the top layer and both kite creases through the top two layers as the flap lifts.
note.petalCreasesHinge: The fold creases the hinge through the top layer as the flap lifts. The kite creases are there already.
note.petalCreasesHingeKite: The fold creases the hinge through the top layer and one kite crease through the top two layers as the flap lifts. The other kite crease is there already.
note.petalCreasesKite: The fold creases one kite crease through the top two layers as the flap lifts. The hinge and the other kite crease are there already.
note.petalCreasesKites: The fold creases both kite creases through the top two layers as the flap lifts. The hinge is there already.
note.petalHingeCrease: Only precreases can be the hinge: one lights up under the pointer.
note.petalHingeCreaseTouch: Only precreases can be the hinge: tap one across the flap.
note.petalRefolds: Every crease it folds is there already: it refolds the hinge and the kite creases.
note.petalRegion: Paper below the hinge lights up where a petal fold can lift it: a click elsewhere says why not.
note.petalRegionTouch: The flap below the hinge lights up once you tap it.
note.rabbitEar: The creases meet at the triangle’s incenter: one to each corner, folded the way you choose, and a fourth the ear rises along, folded the other way.
note.snapPoints: Points snap to corners, marks, crease crossings and midpoints: a click anywhere else picks nothing.
note.snapPointsTouch: Points snap to corners, marks, crease crossings and midpoints: a tap anywhere else picks nothing.
note.squash: A flap squashes when its two layers are free, held only along its hinge, and uncovered, with nothing over it on the side it opens toward.
note.swivelVertex: The creases meet at the dot: the pivot, moved onto the line halfway between the edge and the line it lands on. The bold line is where the edge lands; the lit paper moves, the brightest turning in place.

blocked.steppers: A crease would run into paper that does not fold with it, or paper would hold two parts of the fold together. Step Layers to fold more layers, or Fourth crease to another one.
blocked.swivelEdge: A crease would run into paper that does not fold with it, or paper would hold two parts of the fold together. Pick another pivot, or another line for the edge to land on.
blocked.title: Paper is in the way

center.textEar: The triangle’s creases meet at its incenter, which lies on a crease or off the layers. Pick corners that put it inside the layers, away from their creases.
center.textSwivelEdge: The creases meet where the pivot sits, moved onto the line halfway between the edge and the line it lands on, and that is on a crease or off the paper. Press Esc and pick another pivot.
center.textSwivelStep: The point the creases meet at is on a crease or off the paper. Press Esc and place it again as step 1 says: inside the paper, away from every crease.
center.title: The creases cannot meet there

covered.text: Other layers lie over the flap, or inside it, on the side it opens toward. Fold them out of the way first, or squash it the other way.
covered.title: The flap is covered

fourthBesideStayer.text: The flap rises along the fourth crease, so it lies across from the paper that stays put. Pick another fourth crease, or other paper to stay put.
fourthBesideStayer.title: The fourth crease is beside the paper that stays

fourthCannotRise.text: The fourth crease folds the other way from the other three, and the angles between these creases do not let it. Pick another fourth crease, or other points.
fourthCannotRise.title: The fourth crease cannot rise here

kite.creaseOrPrecrease: Over a hinge crease, a petal fold refolds creases already there, and a kite crease is not. Name the hinge by its two ends instead, and the fold creases the kites itself; or precrease them first, with the Precrease tool on Axiom 3: a lower edge of the top flap onto its centre line, the flaps behind left out.
kite.titleMissing: The kite creases are not there

line.crease: The hinge crease does not run through every layer below it that folds. Precrease the hinge through every layer, then petal fold.
line.ends: The hinge crosses paper of the second layer that folds in beside the kite, and the fold cannot crease that as the flap lifts. Precrease the hinge through every layer, then petal fold.

noFlap.noHinge: The flap folds over no hinge at either end of its spine, so there is nothing to press it flat against.
noFlap.noSpine: The two layers here are not joined by a fold, so the flap has no spine to open along.
noFlap.singleLayer: Only one layer lies here. Click a flap of two layers joined along a folded edge.
noFlap.title: No flap to squash here
noFlap.upperNotHinged: The flap’s top layer is held by its spine alone: pressed flat, its hinge side would lie loose.

noOrder.none: No way of stacking the layers lets it fold flat here. Pick other points, or fold the layers in its way first.
noOrder.otherWay: No way of stacking the layers lets it fold flat this way here. Folded the other way, it fits.
noOrder.rabbitEar: The ear cannot fold flat here
noOrder.squash: It cannot be squashed flat here

noPetal.missesFlap: The flap you clicked lies wholly on one side of the hinge. Click the flap the hinge runs across, or pick a hinge from one of its folded edges to the other.
noPetal.noCornerHinge: The kite creases from the hinge’s ends do not meet below it, so there is no point to lift. Pick a hinge whose ends lie where the kite creases meet the flap’s edges.
noPetal.noEndsHinge: A petal fold’s hinge runs across the flap from one folded edge to the other, and this one crosses one of them, or neither. Pick a hinge whose ends lie on the flap’s two folded edges.
noPetal.noEndsTitle: The hinge does not cross the flap
noPetal.pastCorner: The kite creases from the hinge’s ends meet below it, but the flap reaches past where they meet, and that paper would fold no way. Move the hinge farther from the flap’s closed point: its ends where the kite creases meet the flap’s edges.
noPetal.pastCornerTitle: The hinge is too near the closed point

notFlat.spread: No fourth crease lets these creases lie flat: two of them point the same way, or two neighbours are half a turn or more apart. Press Esc and pick points spread more evenly round the meeting point.
notFlat.swivelEdge: No crease lets the edge turn onto that line and lie flat from this pivot. Press Esc and pick another pivot, or another line.
notFlat.title: It cannot fold flat

notFree.text: The flap is joined to other paper away from its hinge. Only a flap held along its hinge alone opens flat: unfold what holds it first.
notFree.title: The flap is held elsewhere

petalCovered.text: Other layers lie over the flap on the side it lifts toward. Fold them out of the way first, or lift it the other way.
petalCovered.title: The flap is covered

ridgeBesideStayer.pivot: The flap rises along the ridge, so it lies across from the paper that stays put, and here it does not. Pick another pivot.
ridgeBesideStayer.title: The ridge is beside the paper that stays

ridgeCannotRise.pivot: The ridge folds the other way from the other three creases, and the angles between them do not let it. Pick another pivot.
ridgeCannotRise.title: The ridge cannot rise here

stayer.swivelEdge: The paper beside the line, which stays put, is joined to no part of the fold. Pick another pivot, nearer where the edge meets the line.
stayer.text: The paper picked to stay put is joined to no part of the fold. Pick paper the creases cut, or paper joined to it.
stayer.title: Which paper stays?

swivelEdgeShort.text: No part of the edge lies past the point square below the pivot, so none of it would swivel. A plain fold along the line halfway between the edge and its target lays it there instead.
swivelEdgeShort.title: The edge ends before it would turn

swivelEdgeStays.text: The paper along the edge would stay put, or fold across the hinge, rather than turn onto the line. Pick a pivot nearer the edge, or another edge.
swivelEdgeStays.title: The edge would stay put

swivelNotAnEdge.text: A swivel moves a raw edge of the paper or a folded edge, and the line picked is neither. Press Esc and pick the edge again.
swivelNotAnEdge.title: That is no edge

swivelPivotOnEdge.text: The creases meet where the pivot sits, moved onto the line halfway between the edge and the line it lands on, and here that is on the edge itself. Press Esc and pick a pivot farther from where the edge meets the line.
swivelPivotOnEdge.title: The creases would meet on the edge

swivelTargetParallel.text: No turn about a point lays an edge on a line parallel to it, or on its own line. Pick a line that meets the edge’s line.
swivelTargetParallel.title: The line runs parallel to the edge

targetOutside.text: The spine lands between where it lies and the hinge. Click a point inside the flap, or put it back onto the hinge.
targetOutside.title: The spine cannot land there

vertex.ridgesBoth: Either ridge lets it fold flat: step to the other.
vertex.ridgesNone: Neither ridge lets it fold flat: the notice below says why.
vertex.ridgesOne: Only this ridge lets it fold flat.

steps.fanChooseStayer: Choose the fourth crease and the layers. Click other paper to change what stays put.
steps.fanChooseTouch: Choose the fourth crease and the layers. Tap other paper to change what stays put.
steps.finish: Choose the options, then press Enter.
steps.fixOrPickAgain: Click a fix below, or press Esc and pick again.
steps.fixOrPickAgainTouch: Tap a fix below, or tap Cancel and pick again.
steps.petalFinish: Choose Valley or Mountain, then press Enter.
steps.petalFinishTouch: Choose Valley or Mountain, then tap {{action}}.
steps.petalHingeFirstEnd: Click one end of the hinge, where a kite crease meets the flap’s edge.
steps.petalHingeFirstEndTouch: Tap one end of the hinge, where a kite crease meets the flap’s edge.
steps.petalHingeSecondEnd: Click its other end, where the other kite crease meets the edge.
steps.petalHingeSecondEndTouch: Tap its other end, where the other kite crease meets the edge.
steps.petalLiftOther: Valley lifts the flap toward you, Mountain away from you. Click another flap below the hinge to lift that one.
steps.petalLiftOtherTouch: Valley lifts the flap toward you, Mountain away from you. Tap another flap below the hinge to lift that one.
steps.petalRegion: Click the flap below the hinge: the part that lifts lights up under the pointer.
steps.petalRegionTouch: Tap the flap below the hinge, the part that lifts.
steps.pickAgainRead: Press Esc and pick again: the notice below says what to change.
steps.pickAgainReadTouch: Tap Cancel and pick again: the notice below says what to change.
steps.squashTarget: Click where the spine should land, or keep it on the hinge line.
steps.squashTargetTouch: Tap where the spine should land, or keep it on the hinge line.
steps.stayer: Click the paper that stays put.
steps.stayerTouch: Tap the paper that stays put.
steps.swivelChooseRidge: Step Ridge to the other crease that can rise, and choose Valley or Mountain.
steps.swivelEdge: Click the edge that moves: a raw edge or a folded edge.
steps.swivelEdgeTouch: Tap the edge that moves: a raw edge or a folded edge.
steps.swivelFinishRidge: Pick the ridge and the direction, then press Enter.
steps.swivelFinishRidgeTouch: Pick the ridge and the direction, then tap {{action}}.
steps.swivelOnto: Click the line it should land on: a crease or an edge.
steps.swivelOntoFirst: Click a point on the line it should land on.
steps.swivelOntoFirstTouch: Tap a point on the line it should land on.
steps.swivelOntoSecond: Click a second point on that line.
steps.swivelOntoSecondTouch: Tap a second point on that line.
steps.swivelOntoTouch: Tap the line it should land on: a crease or an edge.

vertex.targetHelp: Click the folded paper to land the spine off the hinge.
vertex.targetHelpTouch: Tap the folded paper to land the spine off the hinge.
vertex.valleyTitle: Valley: the paper turns toward you

window.finding: Finding the layers at the line…
window.label: Fold tool options
window.layersHelp: Click a layer to include or exclude its flap. Brackets show where a fold joins two layers.
window.layersHelpWoven: These layers weave through each other, so the stack shown is the one under the pointer. Click a layer to include or exclude its flap.

lengthenColorMode.activeTitle: Extend in the active line type
lengthenColorMode.sameTitle: Extend each crease in its own line type
